newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher on dollar dumping.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher on dollar dumping.

text.p: The won closed stronger versus the dollar on Friday as banks dumped dollars to meet large export negotiations, dealers said.
Some banks also sold the U.S. unit to limit their losses as the won continued to march throughout the day, they said.
The won ended at 824.40 after trading in a wide range of 822.80 to 827.50. It opened at 825.50.
"Banks, fearing a severe shortage of the won, started panic selling (dollars)," said a trader at a major local bank.
Traders said the turnabout in the market sentiment over the dollar surprised most banks.
The won reached an all-time low of 834.50 on Tuesday.
Traders said the won was likely to remain at the current level on Monday. A range of 823 to 827 is seen.
The central bank set the base mid-rate for Monday at 825.00 versus today's 828.90.
